chunks: Abu Sulayman Ahmad ibn Hawtha al-Bahili narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Nahawandi narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari narrated to us, from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal, who said:

Mansur ibn Hazim and Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) while I was present with them, saying: 'May Allah make us ransom for you, indeed souls are taken in the morning and evening, so who will be ours after you?' He said: 'When that happens, this one.' He struck his hand towards the righteous servant Musa, who was a five-year-old boy wearing two white garments, and said: 'This one.' And Abdullah ibn Ja'far was present in the house at that time.

key_terms.الْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: The righteous servant (title for Musa ibn Ja'far)
key_terms.فِدَاكَ: May we be your ransom (a term of high respect)
key_terms.يُغْدَى عَلَيْهَا وَيُرَاحُ: Taken in the morning and evening (referring to death)

ai.seo_question: Who did Imam al-Sadiq designate as his successor?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the explicit designation (Nass) of Musa al-Kazim as the sixth Imam while he was still a young child, highlighting the continuity of divine authority even in the early years of an Imam's life. The presence of key companions like Mansur ibn Hazim and Abdullah ibn Ja'far underscores the communal acceptance of this succession, a critical element in Shia jurisprudence for validating the Imams' infallibility and leadership. The detail of the 'two white garments' is often interpreted by scholars as a sign of purity and distinctiveness, reinforcing the spiritual status of the young Imam.
